content: First arch syndromes are congenital defects caused by a failure of neural crest cells to migrate into the first pharyngeal arch.[1]  They can produce facial anomalies.  Examples of first arch syndromes include Treacher Collins syndrome and Pierre Robin syndrome.
<info> ^ Ronald W. Dudek. High-Yield Embryology. 2e. Page 65.
